examples.text: Die kleine Hähnchenbrust farcieren, mit den gehackten Kräutern, der Frischkrem, dem Eigelb und den Gewürzen zu einer Hackmasse verarbeiten.
„… Ist der Fisch auf einer heißgemachten Schüssel angerichtet, so gibt man eine Kapern- oder Sardellensauce dazu. Auf gleiche Weise kann man auch andere Fische farcieren.“
Den Teig einige Stunden ruhen lassen, dann auf dem Nudelbrett ausrollen und Kreise ausstechen. Mit der Füllung farcieren und halbmondförmig zusammenklappen, die Ränder gut zusammendrücken.
Den Truthahn löffelweise mit den beiden Füllungen farcieren, zuerst die Fleischfüllung fest andrücken und glattstreichen und darüber die Kartoffelfarce. Dann den Bauch zunähen.
Speck und Fleisch/Leberwürfel im Cutter farcieren, die Panade einarbeiten.

glosses: To make full
To add contents to (a container, cavity, or the like) so that it is full.

examples.text: She filled a glass with milk.

My hopes wa'n't disappointed. I never saw clams thicker than they was along them inshore flats. I filled my dreener in no time, and then it come to me that 'twouldn't be a bad idee to get a lot more, take 'em with me to Wellmouth, and peddle 'em out. Clams was fairly scarce over that side of the bay and ought to fetch a fair price.
She continued to frown as she filled Bony's cup and added brandy to her own.
She forgave him the pain as he filled the cavity in her back molar. Three weeks later, she let him fill a more intimate cavity.

Grat Herendeen was the first man, a huge man with his bull whip coiled and over his shoulder seeming almost a part of him. He grinned at her as she filled his plate with the eggs and motioned toward the bacon. "Help yourself, Grat."

glosses: To make full
To enter (something), making it full.

examples.text: The doors opened and guests filled the auditorium.
In the evening of the 14th of July, there was a rainfall of 3 or 3½ inches in that locality. The water filled the ditch so full that it overflowed the levees on both sides in many places […] .
As the crowd filled the aisles, S repeated loudly what he had announced upon entering the stadium: 'I don't want anyone to touch me, and I will call the police if anyone does.'

glosses: To make full
To occupy fully, to take up all of.

examples.text: The smell of spring filled the air.
[…]the drums began to thunder, the sound of trumpets filled the air, the earth trembled beneath their feet, and the hearts of the gazing multitude throbbed with suspense and expectation[…]
And now that I have given the one chapter to the theme that so filled my heart, and so often made it ache and ache again, I pass on, unhindered, to the event that had impended over me longer yet[…].

glosses: To become full.

examples.text: The bucket filled with rain
The room filled with thick smoke.
The sails fill with wind

glosses: To become full.
To become pervaded with something.

examples.text: My heart filled with joy.

glosses: To satisfy or obey (an order, request, or requirement).

examples.text: To qualify for a home loan, you need to fill a number of requirements.
The pharmacist filled my prescription for penicillin.
We can't let the library close! It fills a great need in the community.

glosses: To install someone, or be installed, in (a position or office), eliminating a vacancy.

examples.text: The board of supervisors called a specal election to fill the office, and at such special election Henry C. Andrews was elected judge of probate to fill out the said term.
Sorry, no more applicants. The position has been filled.

glosses: To treat (a tooth) by adding a dental filling to it.

examples.text: Dr. Smith filled Jim's cavity with silver amalgam.

Be that as it may, had the disturbance continued after our having filled the molar, and presuming that nothing had been done to the bicuspid, we might have been still as far as ever from knowing where the trouble lay.

glosses: To block, obstruct

examples.text: The drains were filled with gunk and no water could flow off.

glosses: To supply fully with food; to feed; to satisfy.

examples.text: Are all the children filled and ready for bed?
Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude?
Things that are sweet and fat are more filling.

glosses: To trim (a yard) so that the wind blows on the after side of the sails.
To have sexual intercourse with (a female).

examples.text: Did you fill that girl last night?

glosses: To ejaculate inside someone or something.
A sufficient or more than sufficient amount.

examples.text: Don't feed him any more: he's had his fill.
Then they set somewhat of food before me, whereof I ate my fill, and gave me somewhat of clothes wherewith I clad myself anew and covered my nakedness; after which they took me up into the ship, […]

glosses: An amount that fills a container.

examples.text: The mixer returned to the plant for another fill.

glosses: The filling of a container or area.

examples.text: That machine can do 20 fills per minute.
This paint program supports lines, circles, and textured fills.

glosses: Inexpensive material used to occupy empty spaces, especially in construction.

examples.text: The ruins of earlier buildings were used as fill for more recent construction.
Strippage from a borrow area was first treated as waste, under the contract, but after passage of time was suitable for fill and was so used.

glosses: Soil and/or human-created debris discovered within a cavity or cut in the layers and exposed by excavation; fill soil.
An embankment, as in railroad construction, to fill a hollow or ravine; also, the place which is to be filled.
A short passage, riff, or rhythmic sound that helps to keep the listener's attention during a break between the phrases of a melody.

examples.text: bass fill

The second part of recomposed Embroidering Golden Banner achieves the brightness and cheerfulness of music, and presents a cheerful passion through sanda playing methods such as left-hind octave fills, right-hand echo decoration, and encircled decoration.

glosses: Ellipsis of fill light.
The weft yarn.
One of the thills or shafts of a carriage.

examples.text: It was a challenge to learn to harness him, guide him slowly back between the fills of the carriage, then to fasten the right buckles and snaps, making the harness and buggy all ready for travel to church or to town.

The employees of a business.

examples.text: The company employed 10 new members of staff this month.

glosses: A pole upon which a flag is supported and displayed.

examples.text: I ascend at one [ladder] of six hundred and thirty-nine staves.

glosses: A series of verses so disposed that, when it is concluded, the same order begins again; a stanza; a stave.

examples.text: Mr. Cowley had found out, that no kind of Staff is proper for an Heroick Poem; as being all too lirical:

glosses: An arbor, as of a wheel or a pinion of a watch.

An establishment of officers in various departments attached to an army, to a section of an army, or to the commander of an army. The general's staff consists of those officers about his person who are employed in carrying his commands into execution.

examples.text: At the head of that division which had Westminster Bridge for its approach to the scene of action, Lord George Gordon took his post; with Gashford at his right hand, and sundry ruffians, of most unpromising appearance, forming a kind of staff about him.

glosses: A form of token once used, in combination with a ticket, for safe train movements between two points on a single line.

examples.text: The train-staff and ticket system was used widely at one time, until superseded by electrical token systems, the first of which, the tablet system, appeared in 1878, […].

glosses: To supply (a business, volunteer organization, etc.) with employees or staff members.

glosses: Remplir de farce.

examples.text: Les oreilles de veau ont de commun avec les pieds et les cervelles, l'avantage de pouvoir être frites ou mangées à la poulette ; et de plus elles se laissent farcir, accommoder aux pois, aux oignons, au fromage, etc.

Un jour, Sûzel ayant eu l’idée de chercher en ville une poitrine de veau bien grasse, et de la farcir de petits oignons hachés et de jaunes d’œufs, et d’ajouter à ce dîner des beignets d’une sorte particulière, saupoudrés de cannelle et de sucre, Fritz trouva cela de si bon goût ….

glosses: Remplir avec succès. Il ne s’emploie que dans ces sortes de phrases, et toujours en mauvaise part.

examples.text: Catholiques plus ou moins pratiques, mais presque tous libéraux exaltés, ils arrivaient au congrès la tête farcie des idées américaines sur la séparation de l’Église et de l’État, sur le système fédératif, et autres utopies alors très prônées à la Nouvelle-Grenade.
Il ne cherche pas à rester seul avec moi. Rêve, pauvre fille, rêve, farcis-toi la tête de rêves de pensionnaires, cramponne-toi à tes rêves.
Farcir l’esprit de connaissances inutiles.
Farcir un discours, un plaidoyer de citations.

glosses: Faire quelque chose sans grand plaisir, supporter quelqu'un ou quelque chose de déplaisant.

examples.text: Mais je dois rester, chéri. Hein, dans ce bled ? mais t'es folle ! tu voulais Vegas pas Triffouilly-les-Oies ! Ce contrat tu m'as dit toi-même que c'était juste pour rendre service à ton agent ou à je ne sais plus qui, et que ça te faisait drôlement braire de te farcir cette trotte.
Tu veux mater un Desplechin en te curant le nez peinardos quand l’autre veut te forcer à te farcir Avengers 4.

glosses: Se payer, se régaler de, s’octroyer.

examples.text: On allait se farcir un vrai roupillon d’aventuriers, bien au chaud, confortables, ah ! dis donc.
